items.summaryText:
When managers ask me how to train their nontechnical team on AI, my advice is always the same: run an install party

Everyone brings a laptop & you install the agents right there on their machines & get them to complete a meaningful task on the spot. Skip the abstract talk. Once it's installed, people start talking to the agent and learning from each other

The setup is 80% the barrier

Sandboxes are hard.

With all the “AI escaping  sandbox” it’s easy to think “wow AI so scary,” but most AI companies, and recent “sandbox providers” are making very basic mistakes.

At Replit we’ve been running sandboxes since 2016 and targeted by every hacker and state actor under the sun. So we learned a thing or two. 

Main advice: Assume zero-days exist — because they do — and think in layers of protection in a zero-trust framework.

More here: https://t.co/3XGY0a1p3P

items.summaryText:
The takeaway from this incident should not be that AI is scary. It should be that getting security right is incredibly important in the era of agents. 

Given the right tools and task, agents will do whatever it takes to get the job done, assuming enough compute. Thus, a misconfigured system - or something you thought was locked down but wasn’t - will become a risk vector. 

The core implications are less about the trust and safety of AI itself, but instead the work it’s going to take from enterprises to make sure they harden their environments. Lots of real work ahead for most organizations on this front.

metadata.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

items.summaryZh:
这次事件的教训不应该是 AI 很可怕。而应该是：在智能体时代，把安全做对极其重要。

只要有合适的工具和任务，智能体会不惜一切代价完成任务——只要有足够的算力。因此，一个配置错误的系统——或者你以为已经锁死但实际上没有锁死的系统——就会成为风险向量。

核心影响不在于 AI 本身的信任与安全，而在于企业需要做多少工作来加固自己的环境。多数组织在这件事上还有大量实际工作要做。

items.title: The cost of AI - normalized for the type of task - coming down is one of the mos…
items.summaryText:
The cost of AI - normalized for the type of task - coming down is one of the most important factors in being able to drive further AI diffusion in the economy.

The general trend we should expect is that frontier AI models will continue to become more capable, and will look very expensive because the tasks that they can take on are more advanced. 

Then, shortly after, AI models will get more efficient or competition will drive more aggressive pricing dynamics, thus reducing the cost per task for anything other than the peak of the frontier.

This cycle will continue over and over again, which ultimately leads to tasks becoming cheaper on a like for like basis. And by doing so you will get even more AI adoption because now AI is more affordable for a wider variety of use-cases.

metadata.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

items.summaryZh:
按任务类型归一化后，AI成本的下降是推动AI进一步渗透经济的最重要因素之一。

我们应当预期的总体趋势是，前沿AI模型会继续变得更强大，而且看起来会非常昂贵，因为它们能承担的任务更高级。

随后不久，AI模型会变得更高效，或者竞争会带来更激进的定价动态，从而降低除最前沿顶端以外任何任务的单位成本。

这个循环会反复持续，最终让同类任务的成本越来越低。这样一来，AI的采用会更广泛，因为现在更多类型的用例都能负担得起AI。

Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:21

Speaker 2 | 00:31 - 00:49
Hi. I'm Matt Turk. Welcome to the MAD podcast. My guest today is Sandeep Biswas, cofounder and CEO of Sensera, the $20,000,000,000 company running what might be the largest AI deployment in the physical world. Millions of vehicles, 25,000,000,000,000 data points a year, driving 99% of US roads every single day.

Speaker 2 | 00:49 - 01:14
We talked about physical AI, agents for truckers and frontline workers, humanoids, autonomous trucks, and why the AI boom is really an infrastructure construction project. Oh, and if you're enjoying this episode or if you've liked others in the past, please do us a favor and hit that subscribe button. It takes a second. New episodes will show up right in your feed, and it really helps the podcast. Now here's Sanjit.

Speaker 2 | 01:16 - 01:45
Alright, Sanjit. On this podcast, we've talked a lot about AI models and software agents, but we have spoken a little less about physical AI. So this feels like the episode where we're going to talk about how AI is confronting the physical reality of transportation and construction and plants and utilities. So maybe let's start with physical AI. That's a term that we hear about more and more often these days, and typically in the context of, like, humanoids and robotaxis.

Speaker 2 | 01:45 - 01:48
So from your perspective, what is physical AI?

Speaker 1 | 01:48 - 02:01

Speaker 1 | 02:01 - 02:13

Speaker 1 | 02:13 - 02:33

And that makes it really fascinating because the amount of value that's trapped is really significant. So we think about it in a few different ways. We think about digitizing things like location from GPS tracking, of course.

Speaker 1 | 02:34 - 02:57
We think about using cameras as sensors. So you can use that to understand the physical world in a pretty rich way, especially when you ingest lots and lots of basically video footage. If you think about how many frames you get from that, it's really significant. And then there's a lot of other, kind of data sources, whether that's like weather sources of, like, what happened with precipitation on all the roads. You can think about speed limit data.

Speaker 1 | 02:57 - 03:05
Like, there's lots and lots of physical aspects of the world that when you put them together, when you fuse them together, there's a huge value unlock.

Speaker 2 | 03:05 - 03:27

Speaker 1 | 03:28 - 03:38

Speaker 1 | 03:38 - 03:51
So many of these processes of, how do you maintain a roadway have been in place for a very, very long time. A lot of that process was manual. Right? Like, let's go inspect the condition of the road. Let's understand when it was last worked on.

Speaker 1 | 03:51 - 04:05

Speaker 2 | 04:36 - 05:03
